title: The First Wine & Beer: Chemical Detection of Ancient Fermented Beverages
lineage: Authors’ project site displays scan of publisher article. Read through the web index. Direct download failed. The same authors published the initial 1992 Nature letter.

passages.note: The authors give approximately 3500–2900 BCE for their Period V context.

Yellow deposits in interior crisscross grooves of a double-handled jug tested positive in the Feigl spot test for oxalate. Exterior scrapings and a wine jar sample were negative. The authors infer beer from the assay and vessel analogies, and propose barley because six-row barley dominated sampled botanical remains from Period V.
